Welcome to the Nebius x NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon
Build a working AI system on open, independent infrastructure, and own the whole thing. The NVIDIA x Nebius Global AI Hackathon is for AI builders, ML engineers, founders, and anyone shipping practical, high-performance AI. You'll build with NVIDIA open source models served on Nebius through Nebius Token Factory, on high performance GPU infrastructure. Experiment with new ideas, push the boundaries of open source AI, and submit a project for a chance to win prizes and recognition.

Join fellow builders for technical onboarding, casual workshops, team formation, focused build time, and feedback as you participate in the Global AI Hackathon. Find your nearby city/event here!


Requirements
The Challenge
All submissions must run on either Nebius Token Factory or Nebius AI Cloud and use at least one NVIDIA open source model. Everything else is up to you.

What to Build
Whether it is an app, agent, or something entirely new, your project should fit into one of the following tracks:

Coding and Agentic Engineering Track
Build coding agents and developer tools: agents that write, run, and test code in Token Factory.
Best Apps and Agents Track 
Build any app or agent someone would actually use, from a productivity tool or copilot to a workflow that runs itself. Power it with Nemotron models on Nebius through Token Factory. Reach for Nemotron 3 Ultra when you need serious reasoning, and let Nano or Super handle the fast, everyday calls, so your app stays responsive and your credits stretch further. We encourage you to deploy your application with Nebius Serverless Endpoints, or use Nebius Serverless Jobs for background processing and asynchronous workflows, though neither is required.
Personal AI Track
Build an always-on, private assistant that works for you while keeping your data under your control. Give it persistent memory, reusable skills, access to the tools and information you choose, and the ability to carry out tasks across your daily workflows. Use at least one NVIDIA open source model, and use tools such as NVIDIA NemoClaw, OpenShell, Hermes Agent, and Nebius Serverless to bring personal AI to assemble, secure, and run your own personal AI system.
Physical AI Track
Build embodied and edge agents that sense and act in the real world: robotics, IoT, and on-device intelligence, powered by Nemotron, GROOT, Cosmos and Sonic models and coordinated through an agent runtime. Use Nebius Serverless Jobs to run simulations, generate synthetic data, evaluate robot policies, or process sensor data at scale, and Nebius Serverless Endpoints to serve real-time inference when needed. Your demonstration video must include at least a 1-minute clip showing the physical hardware/robot actually operating, or — if your project has no physical hardware component — the key application modules in action.
What to Submit
A working project. Build something with NVIDIA Nemotron or other NVIDIA open source models on either Nebius Token Factory or Nebius AI Cloud that meets the track requirements.
A category. Pick the track that is the best fit for your project.
A project description. Tell us what you created, why you created it, and how it works.
A working demo. Provide a URL to a working demo, hosted application, or test build of your project.
Not required for Physical AI submissions.
A demo video. Upload a 3-minute or shorter public YouTube video showing your project working — how you used Nebius Token Factory and NVIDIA Nemotron or other NVIDIA open source models. 
Physical AI submissions should include at least one minute of footage showing the physical hardware/robot actually operating, or — if your project has no physical hardware component — the key application modules in action.
A public code repository. Submit a publicly accessible code repository URL (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket) for judging and testing. The repository must include an open source license (such as Apache 2.0, MIT, or MPL 2.0), visible at the top of the repository page.
Include a README with setup instructions and clear guidance for running your project.
Make sure to highlight how you've used NVIDIA Nemotron or other NVIDIA open source models, where Token Factory accelerated your workflow, and any other Nebius Tools or Services used.
Feedback on Nebius Token Factory, AI Cloud, and any NVIDIA tools, models, or technologies used.
If your project existed before the Submission Period, include a written explanation of what was significantly updated during the Submission Period.
If you participated in one of the IRL Builders & Brews events, choose the city you attended for a chance to win the City Winner Award.

# Hermes Home

**Alexa+ on the front. Hermes as the agent underneath.**

> Amazon Developer Hackathon — **Alexa+ track** (self-hosted MCP server, Streamable HTTP, spec 2025-11-25) · also entered in the **Open Source** mini challenge (MIT).

Alexa+ integrates through remote **Streamable-HTTP MCP servers**; the Hermes personal-agent
runtime only ships a stdio MCP server. Hermes Home is the bridge: it exposes a small,
hand-picked set of tools to Alexa+ and keeps every long task asynchronous, so a voice
assistant never waits on a slow agent.

![Alexa+ simulator calling Hermes Home over MCP](docs/img/simulator.jpg)

## Try it in 2 minutes (simulated Alexa+)

No Alexa+ Preview access is needed. `apps/dashboard` contains an **Alexa+ simulator**: a voice/chat
web app that acts as the MCP *client* (official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`), lists the server's tools,
calls them over Streamable HTTP, and shows every `tools/call` in a live trace panel.

```powershell
npm install
copy .env.example .env      # set HERMES_API_URL / HERMES_API_KEY (and PORT if 3000 is busy)
npm run demo                # tunnel -> MCP bridge -> simulator, verified
# open http://127.0.0.1:3100/sim
```

Things to say: *"Ask Hermes what a good question to reflect on today is"* ·
*"Send me a message on Discord with a question to think about"* ·
*"Ask Hermes to plan a productive Saturday"* → *"Is Hermes done?"*

Optional: set `GOOGLE_API_KEY` and the simulator lets Gemini pick tools by function-calling (like real Alexa+);
without it a keyword router is used. Anything that mentions "Hermes" is routed straight to the agent.

## What is exposed (14 tools — never the whole Hermes catalogue)

`hermes_ask` · `hermes_start_task` · `hermes_task_status` · `hermes_task_result` · `home_get_state` ·
`home_control` (two-step confirm) · `hermes_memory_search` · `hermes_remember` · `calendar_today` ·
`calendar_tomorrow` · `calendar_events` · `github_my_issues` · `github_repo_issues` · `send_message`.
Calendar, Home Assistant and GitHub activate when their credentials are in `.env`; otherwise they
return a clear "not configured" result.

# 🐝 Bee Nav

**Say "find me…" to your Bee — get back an answer and directions.**

Bee Nav hears the navigation-style stuff you say out loud to your Bee wearable ("find me a quiet cafe I haven't been to", "take me to a park across town") and turns it into a chosen destination plus a Google Maps route. It uses your *real* Bee data — current location and where you've actually been — so the suggestion is personal, not generic.

```
  🐝 you: "find me a quiet cafe I haven't been to"
        │  Bee CLI / MCP
        ▼
  Bee Nav bridge
        ├── Strands Agents SDK on Amazon Bedrock  (reasoning & tool use)
        ├── get_current_bee_location()            (Bee context)
        ├── get_recent_bee_visits()               (Bee context)
        ├── search_places() ──► Google Places (New)
        └── build_navigation_url() ──► Google Maps
        ▼
  "Lamplight Books & Brew — quiet, 1.4 km away.
   Directions are ready."  →  opens walking route
```

**Privacy, plainly:** your Bee location, visit history, and the utterance are sent to Amazon Bedrock and to Google Places to produce the answer. That's the point of the product — this is not an offline local model, and we don't pretend it is. Nothing is sent anywhere else; the server binds to `127.0.0.1`.

---

## Why "nav"?

Priorities for the Bee track are personal productivity, education, and developer experience. Bee Nav is *personal productivity with the place dimension*: people already use Bee as a memory layer, and the most actionable memory-adjacent question is **"where should I go next?"**. Bee Nav answers it in one shot and hands you the route — no opening three apps, no scrolling a list.

## How the Bee data is actually used (track requirement)

| Bee data | How Bee Nav uses it |
|---|---|
| `bee locations current` | Origin for the Places search + route |
| `bee locations recent` (30-day lookback) |  | **De-duplication**: "haven't been" actually enforces it — won't send you where you went Tuesday |
| `bee now` (recent conversations + utterances) | The bridge polls it for phrases like *"find me / take me / where can I"* and triggers a run |

In code: `src/services/bee.js` shells out to the official Bee CLI (`npm i -g @beeai/cli`, then `bee login`): `bee locations current --json`, `bee locations recent --from <date> --json` and `bee now --json`. A fixture mode (`BEE_SAMPLE=true`) lets anyone run the demo without hardware; the UI labels it loudly.

# What Did I Miss?

A Fire TV AI contextual viewing assistant.

## Credits

Demo film: **Sintel** (c) Blender Foundation | durian.blender.org, licensed [CC BY 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/).
This project is **not endorsed by or affiliated with Blender**. The story index for Sintel (scenes, events, clues) was produced by the project team from the film and is provided for demonstration.

## Problem

People lose track of movies and shows. They check their phone, get interrupted, or simply forget what happened. When they return, they are lost.

## Solution

**What Did I Miss?** is a Fire TV experience that reconstructs the context the viewer missed. It understands:

- exactly what content is playing
- exactly where the viewer is in the timeline
- what was said during the relevant section
- what happened in the current scene
- which earlier story information is relevant
- what characters, objects, clues, and events matter

It never reveals future events. The system behaves like a story-aware memory for television.

## Features

- **Timestamp-aware recap** — knows exactly where you are
- **Spoiler-safe story memory** — never leaks future events
- **Subtitle-aware retrieval** — uses dialogue as data
- **Scene understanding** — connects what happened to where it happened
- **Character/context memory** — tracks who knows what, when
- **Visual context** — uses keyframes for richer understanding
- **Exact missed-range replay** — jump back to the exact moment you missed

- Entrants must create a working software application that runs on either Nebius Token Factory or Nebius AI Cloud and uses at least one NVIDIA open source model, and that fits into one of the four hackathon tracks.

- Judging: 2026-12-01 09:00 PT through 2026-12-15 12:00 PT. Your demo needs to stay working and accessible for that whole period.

- You can get $25 in credits by filling out the Nebius promo form with activation code NEBIUS-DEVPOST-GLOBAL26. A second $25 in Token Factory credit (plus Tavily and other credit) comes from joining the free Nebius Builders Program.

# Nebius x NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon: ideas and plan to win

- **Deadline:** Oct 30, 2026, 10:30 pm IST (10:00 am PT). As of Oct 10 that leaves 20 days.
- **Judging:** Dec 1–15, 2026. The hosted demo must stay up the whole time.
- **Rules page:** https://nebiusglobalaihackathon.devpost.com/rules (text copy in `official-rules.txt`)
- **Credits:** $25 with promo code `NEBIUS-DEVPOST-GLOBAL26`, and another $25 of Token Factory credit plus Tavily credit from the free Nebius Builders Program.

## How projects are scored

1. **Stage 1 (pass/fail):** the project has to be a real attempt at its track, not "a superficial rebrand of an unrelated idea", and it has to make a runtime call to Token Factory, or run on Nebius AI Cloud, with an NVIDIA open model (Nemotron, GR00T, Cosmos or Sonic).
2. **Stage 2 (four criteria, equal weight):**
   - **Technological Implementation:** how well it's built and how well it uses Token Factory and Nemotron. *This criterion also breaks ties.*
   - **Design:** a complete product, not just a proof of concept.
   - **Potential Impact:** a specific, believable case for a real audience, backed by what the demo shows.
   - **Quality of the Idea:** a creative, non-obvious use of the models, and real understanding of the problem.
3. **Prize stacking:** a project wins **one Overall award, OR one Track award plus one Bonus award.** Tavily ($3,000) is a Bonus award, so it stacks with a track win.
4. **Easy money:** 10 × $100 go to the most useful feedback. Write a detailed feedback section.
5. **City award:** you only qualify if you attended an IRL event. None was in India, so skip it.

About 20,000 people have signed up. A public starter ("Hermes Buddy": Vite/React + Hono + Nemotron + Tavily) means a flood of near-identical chat assistants, especially in Personal AI. **Don't build a chatbot.**

---

## Idea 1 (recommended): Greenlight, an agent that does breaking dependency upgrades

**Track:** Coding & Agentic Engineering, plus the **Tavily bonus**

**The problem.** Dependabot and Renovate open version-bump PRs, and the major-version ones break the build. Teams ignore them, and security debt piles up. Every engineer judging this has felt that.

**What it does**
1. Takes a repo and an outdated dependency, for example `pydantic 1 → 2` or `express 4 → 5`.
2. Uses **Tavily** to fetch the changelog, migration guide and GitHub release notes for exactly that version range.
3. **Nemotron 3 Ultra** reads them and writes a migration plan: which APIs changed and which files are affected.
4. **Nemotron Super** makes the code edits.
5. The agent runs install, build and tests in a sandbox (Token Factory sandboxes if they're available, otherwise a Nebius Serverless Job).
6. **Nemotron Nano** shrinks failing logs down to the actual error, and the loop repeats until the tests pass.
7. It opens a PR that says what changed and why, with a link to the source for each change.

**What wins the demo.** A real repo goes from red to green in about 2 minutes, on screen. Next to it, a scoreboard: "Ran 25 real upgrades: 19 green, average $0.04 per upgrade, 71% of tokens on Nano." That routing and cost panel is exactly what the track description asks for ("Ultra for serious reasoning, Nano/Super for everyday calls").

**Why it scores on every criterion**
- *Tech:* the agent runs code, checks it and loops, routes across three model tiers, and makes runtime Tavily calls.
- *Design:* a GitHub App plus a web dashboard. Judges paste a public repo URL and watch it work.
- *Impact:* every software team has this problem, and the eval numbers measure it.
- *Idea:* it reads migration guides from the web. That's a non-obvious reason to need search.

**Risks.** Sandbox time and credit cost. Mitigation: start with **one ecosystem** (Python, or JS/TS) and a curated list of 20–30 real upgrade cases.

---

## Idea 2: Appeal, an agent that fights denied insurance claims

**Track:** Best Apps & Agents, plus the **Tavily bonus**

**The problem.** Insurers deny claims, almost nobody appeals, and a large share of the appeals that do get filed succeed. Pull the current KFF and IRDAI figures before you quote any numbers. The audience is concrete and the stakes are emotional.

**What it does**
1. Takes the denial letter, the EOB and the policy PDF. A Nemotron vision model (Nano VL) pulls out the denial code, the reason and the appeal deadline.
2. **Tavily** finds the insurer's clinical policy, the relevant regulations and the medical guidelines.
3. **Ultra** writes an appeal letter that cites those sources.
4. **Super** produces a checklist of what to get from the doctor.
5. **Nano** tracks the deadline and drafts follow-ups.
6. Optional: run follow-ups as a Nebius Serverless Job.

**What wins the demo.** A real-looking (synthetic) denial goes in, and 60 seconds later out comes a cited appeal letter and a countdown to the deadline.

**Risks.** Medical and legal liability, so present it as a drafting assistant. Use synthetic documents only, never real patient data. It could support the US and India (IRDAI / Insurance Ombudsman) to show reach.

---

## Idea 3: Paper Trail, a private life-admin assistant

**Track:** Personal AI. You have an edge here from Hermes Home, but the track is crowded.

**What it does.** You forward it any bill, warranty, lease, policy or subscription. It remembers all of it (persistent memory) and runs inside **NemoClaw/OpenShell** so the data stays under your control.

It warns you before deadlines: "your warranty expires in 9 days", "the trial converts tomorrow". It also answers questions like "is my laptop still covered?" and drafts the cancel, claim or return email.

Its skills are reusable: cancel-subscription, file-warranty-claim, dispute-charge.

**Why only #3.** The Hermes Buddy starter will flood this track. To stand out you'd need real always-on behaviour (Serverless Jobs on a schedule) and a strong privacy story.

---

## Wildcard: Physical AI

This track gets the fewest entries, so it's the best odds for the Jetson track prize, but the hardest route to the grand prize. If you have no hardware, the rules accept footage of "the key application modules in action". For example, use Cosmos to generate synthetic edge-case footage that evaluates a Nemotron-driven inspection agent, with the batches run as Serverless Jobs. GPU cost against $50 of credit is the risk.

---

## Checklist for whichever idea you pick

- [ ] Route across **Ultra, Super and Nano** on purpose, and **show it in the UI** (tokens, cost and latency per tier).
- [ ] Make at least one runtime **Tavily** call that the product actually depends on.
- [ ] Deploy on **Nebius Serverless Endpoints** and do background work with **Serverless Jobs**. This is extra Nebius usage judges can see.
- [ ] Build an **eval harness** and put the real numbers in the README. "Is the impact credible?" gets answered with data.
- [ ] Hosted demo that **stays up until Dec 15**. Leave credit for it, add rate limits, and include a cached sample run.
- [ ] Public repo with an **MIT/Apache license** visible at the top, and a README with setup steps plus sections titled "How we used Nemotron" and "Where Token Factory helped".
- [ ] **Video under 3 minutes.** Show the result in the first 20 seconds, then how it works, then the numbers.
- [ ] A detailed **feedback section** (10 × $100).
- [ ] Get both $25 credit grants on day 1.

## Rough 20-day plan

| Days | Goal |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Get credits, list the Token Factory models, check that sandboxes exist, build a skeleton that makes one end-to-end call |
| 3–9 | Core agent loop and model routing, plus Tavily |
| 10–13 | Eval harness, run it on the real cases, fix what fails |
| 14–16 | UI polish, hosted deploy, cost panel |
| 17–18 | README, architecture diagram, feedback write-up |
| 19 | Record the video |
| 20 | Submit, with a 1-day buffer before the deadline |

Browser control here means Manu's **own Brave window, profile "Default" (Personal)**, driven through the
**Playwright Extension** (id `mmlmfjhmonkocbjadbfplnigmagldckm`). His logins are there, and he can
watch by opening the agent window, but by default it all runs in the background (see below). Anything else (headless, `--isolated`, T3 preview, `mcp__t3-code__preview_*`) is signed out and
invisible to him, so it is wrong for this job.

## The only correct server config

User-scope MCP server `brave` in `~/.claude.json`:

```
command: node
args: C:\Users\cocat\.local\playwright-mcp\mcp-supervisor.cjs     (supervisor, see below)
      C:\Users\cocat\.local\playwright-mcp\node_modules\@playwright\mcp\cli.js
      --extension
      --executable-path C:/Program Files/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/Application/brave.exe
      --profile-dir-name Default
      --caps vision,pdf,devtools,storage
      --output-dir C:\Users\cocat\.local\playwright-mcp\output
env:  PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXTENSION_TOKEN=<token from the extension>
```

`mcp-supervisor.cjs` (added 2026-10-10) runs cli.js as a child and restarts it transparently when it
dies or when `coreBundle.js` is patched (once idle), replaying the MCP handshake, so open chats never
need `/mcp`. A call running when the child dies gets "The browser server restarted… retry if
needed". Log: `playwright-mcp/supervisor.log`. Test: `node patches/test-supervisor.cjs`. Re-add with
`node patches/use-supervisor.cjs` if the entry is ever rewritten. Chats started before the switch
still run the old command until their next `/mcp` or restart.

**Never** change it to `--headless` or `--isolated`, never drop `--extension` or the token, and never
"fix" a browser problem by switching modes. On 2026-10-09 some session did exactly that, every thread
silently drove an invisible signed-out browser, and Manu couldn't see anything. If you need a throwaway
headless browser for QA, use puppeteer-core in a script, not this server.

## Background mode (never steal Manu's screen)

Manu's rule: browser work must happen silently, never pulling Brave to the front or switching his tab.
Set up on 2026-10-10 (all under `C:\Users\cocat\.local\playwright-mcp\`):

- `extension-bg/`: local build of the extension (same ID/token, loaded unpacked in Brave). It never
  activates tabs, focuses or creates windows (on Windows any new Brave window steals focus). Agent tabs
  are **background tabs** in a collapsed "Playwright" group chip in Manu's window, closed when the MCP
  server disconnects. Rebuild after an extension update with `node patches/build-extension.cjs`, then
  `curl -X POST 127.0.0.1:8770/reload`. If Brave shows "Service worker registration failed" or
  `chrome.X` undefined, he must Remove + Load unpacked again (a plain reload keeps stale settings).
- `broker.cjs` (port 8770, autostarts from `Startup\playwright-broker.vbs`): MCP servers ask it to open
  the connect page through the extension instead of launching `brave.exe` (which always raises Brave).
  `curl 127.0.0.1:8770/status` → `{"extension":true}` when wired up; log in `broker.log`.
- `patches/apply.cjs`: playwright-core patches (re-run after any Playwright update, then `/mcp`):
  broker connect (and never launching `brave.exe` while Brave runs), background new tabs, no
  `bringToFront` on tab switch, instant stable-check and DOM-event clicks/wheel in hidden tabs,
  upload fallback + `browser_set_input_files`. Verified 2026-10-10 on saucedemo (login, add to cart,
  sort) + react-dropzone upload with focus logged: no agent tab ever came to the front.

### Safeguards (what happens when things go wrong)

| Situation | What the setup does | What the agent should do |
|---|---|---|
| Any tool call runs long | Capped at 120 s (`PW_MCP_TOOL_CAP_MS`); page read-back capped at 30 s | Read the error, `browser_snapshot`, continue; never repeat the same call |
| Page stuck in an endless script / hung renderer | After any slow (>4 s) or failed call the tab is pinged; if it doesn't answer in 3 s its JS is terminated, a fresh tab opened and the dead tab closed (also prevents Brave's "Page unresponsive" prompt) | Navigate back and continue |
| Brave freezes the background tab | Hidden agent tabs are kept unfrozen every 2 s | Nothing |
| alert / confirm / prompt | Call returns at once with "Modal state"; self-heal skips tabs with an open dialog | `browser_handle_dialog` |
| Site opens a popup (`target=_blank`, `window.open`, popup window) | Links: default cancelled, URL opened as a background tab. `window.open`: extension switches Manu's tab/window back | Use `browser_tabs` to find it |
| Manu closes the agent's tabs | Connection stays open; next call opens a new tab | Navigate again |
| Extension reloaded / Brave restarted | Next call reconnects through the broker | Retry once |
| Broker dead | Next connect restarts it via `wscript` + `Startup\\playwright-broker.vbs` (detached) | Nothing |
| Extension not connected while Brave runs | Error "background Playwright extension is not connected"; never launches `brave.exe` | Check `curl 127.0.0.1:8770/status`; ask Manu to look at the extension card's Errors |
| Dead host / bad URL | Normal navigation error in <1 s | Report it |

Every stall is appended to `C:\Users\cocat\.local\playwright-mcp\stalls.log`.
**Smoke test** (13 scenarios, real background tabs, checks focus is never taken):
`node C:/Users/cocat/.local/playwright-mcp/patches/smoke.mjs` (add `--skip-disruptive` when other threads
are using the browser: the reload/broker cases briefly drop every agent session). Run it after any
patch, Playwright update or extension rebuild. Last full run 2026-10-10: 13/13 passed except one
non-reproducible focus blip right after the extension-reload case.

**Brave freezes background tabs** (measured: FREEZE 2 s after load, then no timers or network
callbacks, so a site's own JS stalls, e.g. after clicking SEND). `patches/apply.cjs` keeps hidden agent
tabs unfrozen (`Page.setWebLifecycleState active` every 2 s) and caps every tool call at 120 s
(`PW_MCP_TOOL_CAP_MS`). If a call returns "gave up after 120s", take `browser_snapshot` and continue;
don't repeat the call.

**Speed rule: never wait inside the page.** Brave throttles timers in background tabs (≥1 s per
timer, once measured at 7 minutes for a 2 s `setTimeout`). So never put `await new Promise(r =>
setTimeout(r, N))` or polling loops in `browser_evaluate`/`run_code` page functions. Wait with
`browser_wait_for` (`text`, `textGone` or `time`; it waits in Node at full speed) or with Playwright
waits in run_code (`page.waitForSelector`, `locator.waitFor`, `page.waitForURL`), and make evaluate
calls return immediately.

So in agent tabs `document.visibilityState` is normally `"hidden"`; that's expected. In hidden tabs the
patches turn mouse input into DOM events (moves/hover, clicks, double/right clicks, wheel, HTML5
drag-and-drop) and skip the animation-frame/in-page-timer waits Brave throttles there. Verified
2026-10-10 in a real background tab: saucedemo login → cart → checkout (~0.3-1.3 s per tool call),
`browser_drag`, `browser_hover`, `browser_drop` with files, uploads; file pickers opened by clicks are
intercepted (then `browser_file_upload`). Limits: events are untrusted (`isTrusted: false`), CSS
`:hover` styles don't apply, and coordinate clicks don't reach into iframes (use frame locators).
Never call `bringToFront` or start a `brave.exe` yourself. If Manu wants to watch, he can click a tab
in the "Playwright" group. If the server errors with "background Playwright extension is not
connected", check `curl 127.0.0.1:8770/status` and ask Manu to look at the extension card (Errors
button) instead of retrying.

## Hang rule: skip and tell Manu, never keep retrying

A browser tool call that hangs has cost 30 minutes twice (2026-10-09 `mouse.wheel`; 2026-10-10 a
run_code doing `scrollIntoView` + `boundingBox` + `mouse.click` on Do Ventures' SEND, after which the
session dropped and lost its tabs). The `brave` server entry now has `"timeout": 150000` in
`~/.claude.json` (backup `.claude.json.bak-brave-timeout`) so a silent call aborts after 150 s
instead of 30 min; keep it, and don't raise it.

- **Stop signals:** a call that takes more than ~2 min, "gave up after 120s", a tool timeout,
  `Connection closed`, or a connect page / lost tabs after a reconnect. On any of these: do **not**
  retry the same step, loop, or try variants of it. Stop that form/site, mark it
  "skipped (browser hung)" in the tracker/to-do, **tell Manu in the reply**, and move on to the next
  item (or stop if everything else needs the same browser).
- **After a hang you don't know what happened.** Don't resubmit anything. Reopen the page only to
  read state (e.g. a success message), and log the item as "unconfirmed" if you can't see it.
- **Prevent it:** never use `mouse.wheel` (use `window.scrollTo`); keep run_code short (one action
  plus one read, no `scrollIntoView` + coordinate-click chains); click buttons with a plain
  `browser_evaluate` (`el.click()`), which returned instantly where coordinate clicks hung; read
  state with `browser_evaluate`/`browser_snapshot` right after, not inside the same run_code.
- Max one retry of a failed (not hung) step, and only with a different method.

First call in a task: `browser_navigate` to the target, then confirm the session is real:

- the page is signed in (not a login screen) when Manu says he's logged in, and
- `browser_evaluate` → `navigator.userAgent` does **not** contain `HeadlessChrome`.

## Rules

- **Not for email.** Reading, sending or checking mail (Gmail included) goes through `python E:\ai\mailhub\mail.py` (the inbox watcher), never this browser. The only exception is Google's permission screen for the watcher script, when Manu asks.

- Never type Manu's passwords or 2FA codes. If a site is signed out, leave the tab on its login page
  and ask him to sign in there.
- Each client sees only its own tab group, not all of his tabs.
- **File uploads work** (pitch decks, images, PDFs; tested 2026-10-09 on Jotform, Typeform, Airtable,
  Uppy, FilePond, Dropzone, react-dropzone, iframes incl. cross-origin, open/closed shadow DOM, unicode
  filenames, 60 MB byte-exact). Brave rejects the native call (`DOM.setFileInputFiles: Not allowed`), so
  `patches/apply.cjs` makes Playwright read the file in Node and inject it. How to upload:
  0. Folders (`<input webkitdirectory>`): pass the folder path as the only entry in `paths` (either
     tool below); every file underneath is uploaded with its `folder/sub/file` relative path.
  1. `browser_set_input_files` with `target` = snapshot ref or a selector like
     `input[type=file] >> nth=0`, plus absolute `paths`. No click; works on hidden inputs. Inputs inside
     an iframe: `iframe#x >> internal:control=enter-frame >> input[type=file]`.
  2. Widgets with no input until opened (Airtable/Uppy dialog "Drop files here or click to browse"):
     `browser_click` the zone (or `locator.dispatchEvent('click')` in run_code), then step 1 on the new
     input (Airtable: `input.uppy-Dashboard-input:not([webkitdirectory]) >> nth=0`, then press its
     "Upload 1 file" button).
  3. `browser_click` the upload button → "[File chooser]" → `browser_file_upload` (works in background
     tabs too). Drop-only zones: `browser_drop` with `paths`.
  Then confirm in the page (filename/preview/"uploaded") before submitting. Caveats: the page sees
  `isTrusted: false` input/change events (no site tested cared); `accept=` isn't enforced, so pick the
  right file type; sites using `window.showOpenFilePicker` (no `<input>`) can't be automated.
- If uploads fail with "Not allowed", `browser_set_input_files` is missing, or Brave starts jumping to
  the front again, Playwright was reinstalled/updated: re-run
  `node C:/Users/cocat/.local/playwright-mcp/patches/apply.cjs` and restart the server (`/mcp`).
- Other extension limits: animated pages can break the "stable" wait in a visible tab (click by
  coordinates from `getBoundingClientRect`).
- Confirm before anything outward-facing (purchases, publishing, sending, deleting).

> ## Documentation Index > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.tokenfactory.nebius.com/llms.txt > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. # Billing & Consumption ## Set up billing When you sign up for **Nebius Token Factory**, you are prompted to create a **billing account** during onboarding. Billing setup is mandatory—you cannot complete onboarding without it. **Setting up a billing account requires a bank card.** You can view and update your billing details at any time on the **Billing** page. Upon first sign-up, you receive **\$1 in trial credit**, valid for **30 days**. *** ## Payment methods ### Bank card If your payment method is a bank card, you can manually top up your balance at any time. #### Automatic charging When using a bank card, Nebius Token Factory debits your balance in real time. Your card is automatically charged in either of the following cases: * At the start of the month, if your balance is negative * When the configured billing threshold is reached The charge amount is calculated to bring your balance back to zero. If a card charge fails, your account is **suspended**. To avoid service interruptions, ensure that your payment method remains valid and up to date. ### Bank transfer If your payment method is bank transfer, you can top up your balance manually. To do so, request a **proforma invoice** from the Nebius sales team. At the beginning of each month, you will also receive an invoice for the previous month’s usage. If your balance was negative at the end of that month, you must pay the invoice using the payment details provided. > **Note:** Bank transfers are available to companies only and are not supported for individual accounts. ### Changing your payment method * To change your bank card, go to **Organisation → Billing details**, then click **Edit**. * If you are a company, you can switch your payment method to **bank transfer** by contacting support. *** ## Topping up your balance To avoid automatic charging, you can manually top up your balance at any time: 1. Click **Top up** in the top-right corner of the header bar 2. Enter the amount to add, or choose the **Promo code** option 3. Review your card details and click **Continue** Once the top-up is completed, the funds are available immediately. ### Applying a promo code A promo code provides free Nebius Token Factory credits and is typically issued as part of a special offer. Promo codes usually have an expiration date—make sure to apply them before they expire. Promo codes **cannot be used to pay outstanding invoices**. Any unpaid invoices must still be settled separately. To apply a promo code: 1. In the navigation menu, click your **balance** 2. Click **Top up** 3. Select **With promo code** 4. Enter the promo code and click **Top up** After a successful application, your balance increases by the promo code amount.
You can verify this in the **Transactions** section. *** ## Consumption Monitoring You can monitor spending across projects, services, and resources on the **Usage** tab of the **Organisation** page in the web console. To view detailed charts: 1. Click the chart icon on the right 2. Select an entity type and time period using the filters 3. Hover over chart columns to see usage details for a specific period You can further refine results using **region**, **project**, **service**, and **product** filters. *** ## Taxes Depending on your or your company location, the usage of Nebius AI Cloud resources might be subject to taxes such as Value Added Tax (VAT). ### Netherlands Companies registered in the Netherlands and residents of the Netherlands are subject to 21% VAT. VAT amount is listed on invoices on a separate line in USD. We also convert it into EUR and show on another line — it is the same VAT in another currency. ### Another EU country Nebius does not add VAT or other taxes to your charges. VAT amount is calculated in accordance with your country's tax law. It is listed on invoices on a separate line in USD and repeated on another line in EUR. ### United States For residents of Texas and Washington, Nebius calculates taxes in accordance with United States tax law. For details, see [State and Local Sales Tax Rates](https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/sales-tax-rates). Residents of other states are not charged. The tax amount is listed on invoices on a separate line in USD. ### The rest of the world Nebius does not add VAT or other taxes to your charges. At the moment, Nebius does not add VAT or another taxes to your charges. In the future, we will calculate the taxes in accordance with your country tax law. The taxes amount will be listed on invoices on a separate line in USD.

# Greenlight: build plan

> An agent that does the breaking dependency upgrades Dependabot can't. It reads the migration guide, edits the code, runs your tests in a sandbox until they pass, and opens a PR that cites its sources.

- **Track:** Coding & Agentic Engineering, plus the Best Use of Tavily bonus. Both can be won by the same project.
- **Deadline:** Oct 30, 2026, 10:30 pm IST. The internal freeze is **Oct 28**.
- **Judging:** Dec 1–15. The demo must stay up the whole time without costing money.

---

## 1. How we score on each criterion

| Criterion | What judges must see | How Greenlight shows it |
|---|---|---|
| Technological Implementation (also the tiebreaker) | Deep, effective use of Token Factory and Nemotron | A loop across 4 model tiers with a live routing panel. Token Factory **Sandboxes** with checkpoints, and parallel fix attempts branched from one checkpoint. A real Tavily research step. |
| Design | A complete product, not a proof of concept | A polished web app: pick a repo, watch red turn green live, get a PR. Plus a CLI and a public scoreboard. |
| Potential Impact | A credible, specific audience, backed by the demo | Real open-source repos stuck on pydantic 1, numpy 1 or pandas 1. The **eval numbers** (X of N upgraded, $/upgrade, minutes/upgrade) are the evidence. |
| Quality of the Idea | Non-obvious use; real understanding of the problem | The search step is needed because migration guides live on the web. Anti-cheat checks show we know how agents game tests. |

**Stage 1 pass/fail:** at runtime it calls Token Factory with Nemotron, and it's clearly a coding agent that "writes, runs, and tests code".

---

## 2. What the demo shows (the video script drives the build)

1. Paste a repo, for example `someorg/somerepo`, and the dependency `pydantic → 2.x`.
2. **Baseline:** clone into the sandbox, install, run tests, and show the green baseline (N tests).
3. **Bump:** change the version pin, run tests, and show them go **red**: 37 failures, grouped by cause.
4. **Research:** Tavily fetches the official migration guide and the changelog for that exact version range. Cards show the sources.
5. **Plan:** Nemotron 3 Ultra maps each failure group to a migration rule and a list of files.
6. **Fix:** Nemotron Super edits code with tools. Nano or Lightning condenses the test logs. 2–3 attempts run **in parallel** from one sandbox checkpoint, and the best one is kept.
7. **Verify:** the tests go green. The anti-cheat panel shows: the target version is installed, no test files were edited, the test count didn't drop, and nothing new is skipped.
8. **Ship:** a PR on a fork, with a migration note that cites a guide section for each change.
9. **Receipts:** the routing panel (tokens, $ and latency per model) and a link to the scoreboard, e.g. "19/25 real upgrades green, median $0.06, median 4 min".

---

## 3. Architecture

```
┌──────────── web (Vite + React + TS) ────────────┐   ┌── CLI (greenlight upgrade …) ──┐
│ run page (SSE stream) · scoreboard · replays    │   │ same core, local terminal UI   │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘   └───────────────┬────────────────┘
                        │ HTTP + SSE                                   │
┌───────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────────▼───────────────┐
│ server (Python 3.12, FastAPI)  ── run queue · event log (JSONL) · replay store       │
│ core/                                                                                │
│   orchestrator.py   state machine: baseline → bump → research → plan → fix ⟲ → verify│
│   llm.py            OpenAI-compatible client → Token Factory; model router; BUDGET   │
│   research.py       Tavily search + extract → cached "migration rule sheet"          │
│   executor/         Executor interface                                               │
│       contree.py      Token Factory Sandboxes (primary)                              │
│       docker.py       local Docker (dev + fallback)                                  │
│   tools.py          read_file · grep · apply_patch · run_tests · list_failures       │
│   verify.py         anti-cheat checks                                                │
│   pr.py             git commit + PR to fork (gh / GitHub API)                        │
│ evals/              dataset.yaml · runner · scoreboard.json                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │ Token Factory API (Nemotron)      │ Sandboxes API         │ Tavily API
```

**Why Python:**
- The Sandboxes SDK (`contree-sdk`) is Python-only.
- Tavily and the OpenAI client are first-class in Python.
- The target repos are Python.
- The frontend is TypeScript (React), built to static files and served by FastAPI. That's one container.

---

## 4. The agent loop (orchestrator)

1. **Prepare:**
   - Pull a `python:3.12` image with git and uv, and checkpoint it as the "toolchain image".
   - Clone the repo at the pinned SHA, then checkpoint ("repo image").
2. **Baseline:**
   - Detect the manifest (`requirements*.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg/py`), the test command (pytest or unittest) and the Python version.
   - `uv pip install`, then run the tests with `--junitxml`.
   - Record the set of tests that pass at baseline. That set is the contract. If the baseline is red, run "only fix the previously passing tests" and say so.
3. **Bump:**
   - Rewrite the pin to the target range and install.
   - Confirm the installed version with `pip show`, then run the tests. This gives the failing tests.
   - Checkpoint ("bumped image").
4. **Triage:** Nano/Lightning groups the failures by root cause (exception type, frame, symbol). That compresses 500 KB of logs into roughly 3 KB of grouped failures.
5. **Research:**
   - Tavily `search` restricted to the official domains first (pydantic.dev, numpy.org, pandas.pydata.org, docs.sqlalchemy.org, github.com releases), with a fallback to open search.
   - Tavily `extract` pulls the guide pages.
   - Nano/Lightning turns the pages into a **rule sheet**: old API → new API, with the source URL and section anchor for each rule.
   - The rule sheet is cached per (library, from, to), so a repeat run costs nothing.
   - Grep the repo for every "old API" in the rule sheet. This finds call sites the tests don't cover too.
6. **Plan:** Ultra gets the grouped failures, the rule sheet and the grep hits. It returns a structured plan: a list of edits, each with file, rule ID and rationale.
7. **Fix:**
   - Super runs a tool-calling loop over `read_file / grep / apply_patch / run_tests`.
   - Edits use search/replace blocks, with no whole-file rewrites.
   - **Parallel attempts:** branch 2–3 sandboxes from the bumped checkpoint, each with a different plan slice or temperature. Keep whichever one has the most baseline tests passing.
8. **Loop:**
   - After each test run, Nano condenses the new failures.
   - If there's no progress in 2 iterations, **escalate to Ultra** to re-plan.
   - Hard stops: 6 iterations, a $ budget for the run, or 15 minutes.
9. **Verify** (`verify.py`):
   - Every baseline-passing test passes now.
   - The installed version matches the target.
   - No test file was changed, unless the user allows it.
   - No new `skip`/`xfail`, and the test count didn't drop.
   - No pin rolled back, and no `# type: ignore` / `noqa` spam.
   - The diff is in the same files as the evidence.
10. **Ship:**
    - Write the PR body: summary, a table of changes with a guide citation each, test evidence before and after, and a cost line.
    - Open the PR against **our fork**. The default is a draft PR; never upstream unless the owner asks.

---

## 5. Model routing (IDs checked live with our key on 2026-10-10)

| Role | Model | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Planner, plus escalation when stuck | `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b` | Hardest reasoning, but called rarely (1–3× per run) |
| Code editor (tool loop) | `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` | Strong tool calling at about a third of Ultra's price |
| Log triage, doc digestion, PR text | `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B` **or** `nvidia/Nemotron-3_5-Lightning` | Cheap and fast; whichever wins the day-1 bake-off |

- Prices: read the exact per-token prices from the `/organization/prices` page on day 1 and keep them in `prices.json`. The research agent's figures for Ultra are $1.00/$3.00 and for Super $0.30/$0.90 per 1M tokens in/out. Verify both.
- **Thinking mode:** Nemotron 3 thinks by default. Calls that need no reasoning send `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}`, and planner calls leave it on. Leaving `max_tokens` too low can return empty `content`, so verify this on day 1.
- The UI panel shows every call: model, purpose, tokens in/out, $, latency and thinking on/off. The summary line looks like: "Ultra 4% of tokens / 31% of $".

---

## 6. Budget guard: never charge the card (top priority)

Token Factory is **postpaid**, so the card is charged if the balance goes negative, and no cap exists on Nebius's side. So:

- `llm.py` estimates the worst-case cost of every call **before sending it**: input tokens plus `max_tokens` at that model's price.
- It adds the real cost to a **persistent ledger** (`~/.greenlight/ledger.jsonl`, plus a mirror on the server) after each call.
- **Global cap:** `GREENLIGHT_BUDGET_USD=20` by default. The balance is $30.50, so that leaves $10 of headroom. A call that would cross the cap raises `BudgetExceeded` and the run stops cleanly.
- **Per-run cap:** $0.75 by default.
- **Daily cap:** $5 by default.
- Tavily has 9,000 credits, its own counter and a cap of 7,000.
- **Public demo:** judges get **replay mode** by default, which plays back recorded runs exactly and costs $0.
  - Live mode is limited to the curated cases.
  - It needs an access code, which goes in the Devpost testing notes.
  - It's rate-limited to 1 concurrent run and 10 runs per day.
- Credits are added only through promo codes or the Builder Program. Keys get revoked after Dec 15.
- `greenlight budget` prints spend so far against the cap.

---

## 7. Where code runs

- **Primary: Token Factory Sandboxes** (Contree). Beta access was requested on 2026-10-10. It's free in beta, and it's what the track text literally names.
  - Used through REST: `POST /sandboxes/v1/instances` and poll the operation, or through `contree-sdk`.
  - Checkpoints are needed for: the toolchain image, then the repo, then the bumped state, then parallel branches.
- **Fallback: local Docker executor** behind the same `Executor` interface. Used for development until access is granted, and as an offline mode for the CLI.
- **Day-1 check, once access is granted:** confirm that `git clone`, `pip`/`uv install` and pytest work inside a sandbox and that outbound network access works.
- If Sandboxes access never arrives, Docker stays the executor. The claim then becomes "runs Nemotron on Token Factory" only, which still passes Stage 1. The video explains the executor interface.

---

## 8. Test set and scoreboard

- `evals/dataset.yaml`: 25–30 real repos pinned at a commit, each with a library, `from → to`, a test command, and a timeout. Candidates come from `research/eval-candidates.md` (in progress).
- Mix: about 10 pydantic 1→2, about 8 numpy 1→2, about 8 pandas 1→2, plus a few SQLAlchemy 1.4→2.0 as stretch cases.
- Each case gets a **pre-check** first: does the baseline go green, and does the bump go red? Cases that fail the pre-check are dropped and the reason is logged. That keeps the eval honest.
- Metrics: green rate, partial rate (≥80% of baseline tests passing), median $, median minutes, iterations, tokens by tier, and the escalation rate.
- **Ablations**, for the judges:
  - All-Ultra against routed: same success rate, X× cheaper?
  - Without Tavily research against with it: this shows the search is actually needed.
  - These numbers go in the README and the video.
- Results are published as `scoreboard.json`, which drives the scoreboard page. Every green case links to its PR on our fork.

---

## 9. Hosting (free, no card)

- **Hugging Face Spaces (Docker, free CPU)** hosts the FastAPI and static UI container. It needs no card, has long-running processes and an HTTPS URL.
  - It sleeps after about 48 h idle. Ping it with a GitHub Actions cron during judging.
- **Not** Nebius Serverless Endpoints. Those bill to AI Cloud, a separate billing account and a card risk. Explain why in the feedback section.
- Replay files ship inside the image, so the demo works even if every key is revoked.

---

## 10. Repo layout (public GitHub, MIT)

```
greenlight/
  LICENSE (MIT)  README.md  FEEDBACK.md  Dockerfile  pyproject.toml
  greenlight/        core python package (orchestrator, llm, research, executor, tools, verify, pr, cli)
  server/            FastAPI app (runs, SSE, replays, scoreboard API)
  web/               Vite + React + TS UI
  evals/             dataset.yaml, runner, results/, scoreboard.json
  replays/           recorded runs used by the public demo
  tests/             unit tests for the core (verify.py and the budget guard are tested hardest)
  docs/              architecture.png, demo script, judge notes
```

The README needs these sections: "How we use Nemotron", "Where Token Factory accelerated us", "Tavily", "Sandboxes", "Results", "Run it yourself", "What's new during the submission period".

---

## 11. Schedule: 20 days, with checkpoints

| Dates | Milestone | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **Oct 10–11** | Foundations | Repo scaffold. `llm.py` with routing, the budget guard and its tests. Thinking-toggle check. Model bake-off (Nano vs. Lightning). Prices recorded. Docker executor. |
| **Oct 12–14** | Vertical slice | One pydantic repo goes from red to green end-to-end in the CLI (Docker executor), with a verify pass. |
| **Oct 15–17** | Research and robustness | Tavily rule sheets and cache. Grep for call sites. Escalation. Parallel attempts. Contree executor (if access granted). |
| **Oct 18–20** | Eval v1 | Dataset pre-checked. Full eval run. Fix the top failure modes. Scoreboard v1. |
| **Oct 21–23** | Product | Web UI (run page, routing panel, anti-cheat panel, diff view, scoreboard). Replay recording. PRs on forks. |
| **Oct 24–25** | Ship infra | HF Spaces deploy, access code, rate limits, cron keep-alive. Eval v2 with ablations. |
| **Oct 26–27** | Story | README, architecture diagram, FEEDBACK.md, record and edit the video (≤3 min). |
| **Oct 28** | **Freeze** | Devpost draft complete. A full test of the judge path in a clean browser. |
| Oct 29–30 | Buffer | Submit by Oct 29 evening IST. |

**Go/no-go checks:**
- **Oct 14:** if there's no end-to-end green yet, cut parallel attempts and SQLAlchemy.
- **Oct 20:** if the green rate is under 40%, narrow to pydantic only and lead with depth.

---

## 12. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Sandboxes access is slow or denied | The Docker executor behind the same interface. Only the claim changes. |
| The card gets charged | Budget guard, replay-first demo, promo-only top-ups, key revocation |
| Agent "passes" by gaming the tests | `verify.py` checks, shown in the UI |
| Low green rate | Pre-filtered dataset, rule sheets, escalation and parallel attempts. Report partial results honestly. |
| Nemotron returns empty content with thinking on | Toggle thinking per call; budget `max_tokens`; retry once with thinking off |
| Rate limits (60 RPM / 400K TPM baseline) | One live run at a time; eval runs in serial batches with backoff |
| Repos need services or heavy builds | Pre-check drops them |
| HF Space sleeps during judging | Cron ping; replay files are static, so even a cold start works |

---

## 13. Defaults chosen, to change only if Manu objects

- PRs go to **forks under `manuvamp`**, as drafts, never upstream.
- Hosting is on **Hugging Face Spaces**. That needs an HF account, which would be created with GitHub login later.
- **MIT** license.
- The repo name is `greenlight-agent` (public), created when the vertical slice works.
- Budget caps are $20 global, $5/day and $0.75/run.

"""Nemotron models on Nebius Token Factory, their prices, and which job each one does.

Prices are USD per 1M tokens, read from tokenfactory.nebius.com/endpoints on 2026-10-10.
If Nebius changes them, update this table: the budget guard prices every call from it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Model:
    id: str
    label: str
    usd_in_per_m: float
    usd_out_per_m: float

    def cost(self, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int) -> float:
        return (tokens_in * self.usd_in_per_m + tokens_out * self.usd_out_per_m) / 1_000_000


ULTRA = Model("nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b", "Nemotron 3 Ultra", 1.00, 3.00)
SUPER = Model("nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b", "Nemotron 3 Super", 0.30, 0.90)
LIGHTNING = Model("nvidia/Nemotron-3_5-Lightning", "Nemotron 3.5 Lightning", 0.06, 0.24)
NANO = Model("nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B", "Nemotron 3 Nano", 0.06, 0.24)

ALL = {m.id: m for m in (ULTRA, SUPER, LIGHTNING, NANO)}


class Role(str, Enum):
    """What a call is for. The router maps each role to a model."""

    PLAN = "plan"          # read failures + migration rules, decide the edits
    ESCALATE = "escalate"  # re-plan after the editor stalls
    EDIT = "edit"          # tool-calling loop that changes code
    TRIAGE = "triage"      # condense test logs into grouped failures
    DIGEST = "digest"      # turn migration-guide pages into a rule sheet
    WRITE = "write"        # PR description, summaries


ROUTES: dict[Role, Model] = {
    Role.PLAN: ULTRA,
    Role.ESCALATE: ULTRA,
    Role.EDIT: SUPER,
    Role.TRIAGE: LIGHTNING,
    Role.DIGEST: LIGHTNING,
    Role.WRITE: LIGHTNING,
}

# Reasoning ("thinking") is on by default in Nemotron 3. Only the roles that need it keep it.
THINKING: dict[Role, bool] = {
    Role.PLAN: True,
    Role.ESCALATE: True,
    Role.EDIT: False,
    Role.TRIAGE: False,
    Role.DIGEST: False,
    Role.WRITE: False,
}


def route(role: Role, override: str | None = None) -> Model:
    """Model for a role. `override` (a model id) forces one model, e.g. for the all-Ultra ablation."""
    if override:
        return ALL[override]
    return ROUTES[role]

"""Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory: routed, priced, and capped.

Every call:
  1. picks a model from the role (models.route),
  2. reserves its worst-case cost with the budget guard (refused if it would cross a cap),
  3. calls the OpenAI-compatible Token Factory API,
  4. settles the real cost from `usage` and emits a CallRecord for the routing panel.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable

import openai
from openai import OpenAI

from .budget import Budget
from .models import ALL, THINKING, Model, Role, route

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("NEBIUS_BASE_URL", "https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/")

# Conservative token estimate for the pre-call reservation: ~3 chars per token
# (code and JSON tokenize denser than English prose).
CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3


class LLMError(RuntimeError):
    pass


class LLMTruncated(LLMError):
    """The model hit max_tokens before producing an answer (usually all spent on reasoning)."""


@dataclass
class CallRecord:
    run: str
    role: str
    model: str
    thinking: bool
    tokens_in: int
    tokens_out: int
    usd: float
    latency_s: float
    ok: bool
    note: str = ""
    ts: float = field(default_factory=time.time)


@dataclass
class LLMResult:
    content: str
    tool_calls: list[dict]
    reasoning: str
    finish_reason: str
    record: CallRecord
    raw_message: dict

    def json(self) -> Any:
        """Parse `content` as JSON, tolerating a ```json fence."""
        text = self.content.strip()
        if text.startswith("```"):
            text = text.split("\n", 1)[1] if "\n" in text else ""
            text = text.rsplit("```", 1)[0]
        return json.loads(text)


def estimate_tokens(*parts: Any) -> int:
    chars = sum(len(p if isinstance(p, str) else json.dumps(p, default=str)) for p in parts if p)
    return chars // CHARS_PER_TOKEN + 16


class LLM:
    def __init__(
        self,
        budget: Budget | None = None,
        api_key: str | None = None,
        model_override: str | None = None,
        timeout: float = 180.0,
    ):
        key = api_key or os.environ.get("NEBIUS_API_KEY")
        if not key:
            raise LLMError("NEBIUS_API_KEY is not set")
        self.client = OpenAI(base_url=BASE_URL, api_key=key, timeout=timeout, max_retries=0)
        self.budget = budget or Budget()
        self.model_override = model_override
        self.listeners: list[Callable[[CallRecord], None]] = []

    def on_call(self, fn: Callable[[CallRecord], None]) -> None:
        self.listeners.append(fn)

    def _emit(self, rec: CallRecord) -> None:
        for fn in self.listeners:
            try:
                fn(rec)
            except Exception:
                pass

    def chat(
        self,
        role: Role,
        messages: list[dict],
        *,
        run: str,
        tools: list[dict] | None = None,
        tool_choice: str | dict | None = None,
        max_tokens: int = 2048,
        thinking: bool | None = None,
        temperature: float | None = None,
        json_mode: bool = False,
        retries: int = 2,
    ) -> LLMResult:
        model = route(role, self.model_override)
        think = THINKING[role] if thinking is None else thinking
        last_err: Exception | None = None
        for attempt in range(retries + 1):
            try:
                return self._call_once(model, role, messages, run, tools, tool_choice,
                                       max_tokens, think, temperature, json_mode)
            except (openai.RateLimitError, openai.APIConnectionError, openai.InternalServerError) as e:
                last_err = e
                time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1) ** 2)
        raise LLMError(f"{model.id} failed after {retries + 1} attempts: {last_err}")

    def _call_once(self, model: Model, role: Role, messages, run, tools, tool_choice,
                   max_tokens, think, temperature, json_mode) -> LLMResult:
        est_in = estimate_tokens(messages, tools)
        worst = model.cost(est_in, max_tokens)
        res = self.budget.reserve(run=run, kind="llm", label=f"{role.value}:{model.id}", usd=worst)

        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
            "model": model.id,
            "messages": messages,
            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "extra_body": {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": think}},
        }
        if tools:
            kwargs["tools"] = tools
            if tool_choice:
                kwargs["tool_choice"] = tool_choice
        if temperature is not None:
            kwargs["temperature"] = temperature
        if json_mode:
            kwargs["response_format"] = {"type": "json_object"}

        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            resp = self.client.chat.completions.create(**kwargs)
        except (openai.BadRequestError, openai.AuthenticationError,
                openai.PermissionDeniedError, openai.NotFoundError, openai.RateLimitError) as e:
            # Rejected before any generation: nothing was billed.
            res.settle(usd=0.0, model=model.id, error=type(e).__name__)
            self._emit(CallRecord(run, role.value, model.id, think, 0, 0, 0.0,
                                  time.monotonic() - t0, False, type(e).__name__))
            raise
        except Exception as e:
            # Unknown outcome (timeout, dropped connection): assume the worst case was billed.
            res.settle(usd=worst, model=model.id, error=type(e).__name__, assumed=True)
            self._emit(CallRecord(run, role.value, model.id, think, est_in, max_tokens, worst,
                                  time.monotonic() - t0, False, type(e).__name__))
            raise
        latency = time.monotonic() - t0

        usage = resp.usage
        tin = getattr(usage, "prompt_tokens", None) or est_in
        tout = getattr(usage, "completion_tokens", None)
        if tout is None:
            tout = max_tokens
        usd = model.cost(tin, tout)
        res.settle(usd=usd, model=model.id, tokens_in=tin, tokens_out=tout)

        choice = resp.choices[0]
        msg = choice.message
        msg_dict = msg.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
        content = msg.content or ""
        reasoning = msg_dict.get("reasoning_content") or msg_dict.get("reasoning") or ""
        tool_calls = [tc.model_dump() for tc in (msg.tool_calls or [])]
        finish = choice.finish_reason or ""

        rec = CallRecord(run, role.value, model.id, think, tin, tout, usd, latency, True, finish)
        self._emit(rec)

        if finish == "length" and not content.strip() and not tool_calls:
            raise LLMTruncated(
                f"{model.id} spent all {max_tokens} tokens without answering (thinking={think})"
            )
        return LLMResult(content, tool_calls, reasoning, finish, rec, msg_dict)


def record_to_dict(rec: CallRecord) -> dict:
    d = asdict(rec)
    d["model_label"] = ALL[rec.model].label if rec.model in ALL else rec.model
    return d

import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pytest

from greenlight.budget import Budget, BudgetExceeded, Caps


def make(tmp_path, **caps):
    return Budget(home=tmp_path, caps=Caps(**{"usd_total": 1.0, "usd_daily": 1.0, "usd_per_run": 1.0, **caps}))


def test_reserve_and_settle_counts_actual_cost(tmp_path):
    b = make(tmp_path)
    r = b.reserve(run="r1", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.5)
    assert b.totals().usd_total == pytest.approx(0.5)
    r.settle(usd=0.1)
    t = b.totals()
    assert t.usd_total == pytest.approx(0.1)
    assert t.open_reservations == 0


def test_global_cap_refuses_before_spending(tmp_path):
    b = make(tmp_path, usd_total=1.0)
    b.reserve(run="a", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.6).settle(usd=0.6)
    with pytest.raises(BudgetExceeded, match="global cap"):
        b.reserve(run="b", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.5)
    # the refused call left no trace in the totals
    assert b.totals().usd_total == pytest.approx(0.6)


def test_per_run_cap(tmp_path):
    b = make(tmp_path, usd_per_run=0.3)
    b.reserve(run="a", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.2).settle(usd=0.2)
    with pytest.raises(BudgetExceeded, match="per-run cap"):
        b.reserve(run="a", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.2)
    # a different run is still allowed
    b.reserve(run="b", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.2)


def test_daily_cap_ignores_older_days(tmp_path):
    b = make(tmp_path, usd_daily=0.5, usd_total=10)
    old = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=2)).isoformat()
    with b.ledger.open("a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({"type": "reserve", "id": "old", "ts": old, "run": "z", "kind": "llm",
                            "label": "x", "usd": 3.0, "credits": 0}) + "\n")
        f.write(json.dumps({"type": "settle", "id": "old", "ts": old, "usd": 3.0, "credits": 0}) + "\n")
    t = b.totals()
    assert t.usd_total == pytest.approx(3.0)
    assert t.usd_today == pytest.approx(0.0)
    b.reserve(run="n", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.4)
    with pytest.raises(BudgetExceeded, match="daily cap"):
        b.reserve(run="n2", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.2)


def test_unsettled_reservation_keeps_counting_at_estimate(tmp_path):
    """A crash between reserve and settle must make the guard stricter, not looser."""
    b = make(tmp_path, usd_total=1.0)
    b.reserve(run="a", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.9)  # never settled
    b2 = Budget(home=tmp_path, caps=b.caps)  # new process
    assert b2.totals().open_reservations == 1
    with pytest.raises(BudgetExceeded):
        b2.reserve(run="b", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.2)


def test_tavily_credit_cap(tmp_path):
    b = make(tmp_path, tavily_credits_total=3)
    b.reserve(run="a", kind="tavily", label="search", credits=2).settle(credits=2)
    with pytest.raises(BudgetExceeded, match="Tavily"):
        b.reserve(run="a", kind="tavily", label="search", credits=2)


def test_settle_twice_is_noop(tmp_path):
    b = make(tmp_path)
    r = b.reserve(run="a", kind="llm", label="x", usd=0.2)
    r.settle(usd=0.1)
    r.settle(usd=0.9)
    assert b.totals().usd_total == pytest.approx(0.1)


def test_negative_estimate_rejected(tmp_path):
    b = make(tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        b.reserve(run="a", kind="llm", label="x", usd=-1)

"""Day-1 check of every Nemotron model on Token Factory.

Checks: plain answer with thinking off/on, tool calling (Super, Lightning, Nano), JSON mode.
Prints one line per call with tokens, cost and latency. Every call goes through the budget guard.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys

from greenlight.config import load_env

load_env()

from greenlight.llm import LLM, LLMError  # noqa: E402
from greenlight.models import LIGHTNING, NANO, SUPER, ULTRA, Role  # noqa: E402

RUN = "smoke-models"
results: list[dict] = []

TOOL = [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "apply_patch",
        "description": "Replace an exact snippet in a file.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "path": {"type": "string"},
                "search": {"type": "string"},
                "replace": {"type": "string"},
            },
            "required": ["path", "search", "replace"],
        },
    },
}]

CODE = "from pydantic import BaseModel, validator\n\nclass User(BaseModel):\n    name: str\n\n    @validator('name')\n    def strip(cls, v):\n        return v.strip()\n"


def show(tag: str, fn):
    try:
        r = fn()
        rec = r.record
        out = (r.content or json.dumps(r.tool_calls)[:160]).replace("\n", " ")[:120]
        print(f"OK   {tag:38s} in={rec.tokens_in:5d} out={rec.tokens_out:5d} ${rec.usd:.5f} "
              f"{rec.latency_s:5.1f}s fin={r.finish_reason:10s} reasoning={len(r.reasoning):5d}ch | {out}")
        results.append({"tag": tag, "ok": True, **rec.__dict__, "content": r.content[:400],
                        "tool_calls": r.tool_calls, "reasoning_chars": len(r.reasoning)})
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"FAIL {tag:38s} {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:200]}")
        results.append({"tag": tag, "ok": False, "error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"})


def main() -> int:
    llm = LLM()
    q = [{"role": "user", "content": "In one short sentence: what replaced pydantic v1's @validator in v2?"}]

    for model in (ULTRA, SUPER, LIGHTNING, NANO):
        llm.model_override = model.id
        show(f"{model.label} think=off", lambda: llm.chat(Role.WRITE, q, run=RUN, max_tokens=120, thinking=False))
    for model in (ULTRA, SUPER, LIGHTNING):
        llm.model_override = model.id
        show(f"{model.label} think=on (1200)", lambda: llm.chat(Role.PLAN, q, run=RUN, max_tokens=1200, thinking=True))

    edit = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You migrate Python code from pydantic v1 to v2. Use the apply_patch tool. Make one patch."},
        {"role": "user", "content": f"File app/models.py:\n```python\n{CODE}```\nMigrate the validator to pydantic v2."},
    ]
    for model in (SUPER, LIGHTNING, NANO):
        llm.model_override = model.id
        show(f"{model.label} tools", lambda: llm.chat(Role.EDIT, edit, run=RUN, tools=TOOL, max_tokens=600, thinking=False))

    js = [{"role": "user", "content": 'Return JSON {"old": string, "new": string} for the v1->v2 rename of .dict() in pydantic.'}]
    for model in (SUPER, LIGHTNING):
        llm.model_override = model.id
        show(f"{model.label} json", lambda: llm.chat(Role.DIGEST, js, run=RUN, max_tokens=200, thinking=False, json_mode=True))

    t = llm.budget.totals()
    print(f"\nrun spend ${t.usd_by_run.get(RUN, 0):.5f} | ledger total ${t.usd_total:.5f} | open reservations {t.open_reservations}")
    with open("scripts/smoke_models.out.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=2, default=str)
    return 0 if all(r["ok"] for r in results) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

from greenlight.manifest import bump_text, mentions

SPEC = ">=2,<3"


def test_requirements_pinned():
    out, ch = bump_text("fastapi==0.95\npydantic==1.10.13\nrequests\n", "pydantic", SPEC, "requirements.txt")
    assert "pydantic>=2,<3\n" in out
    assert "fastapi==0.95" in out
    assert ch == [("pydantic==1.10.13", "pydantic>=2,<3")]


def test_requirements_extras_marker_comment():
    src = "pydantic[email] < 2 ; python_version >= '3.8'  # pinned\n"
    out, ch = bump_text(src, "pydantic", SPEC, "requirements.txt")
    assert out.startswith("pydantic[email]>=2,<3 ; python_version >= '3.8'")
    assert "# pinned" in out
    assert len(ch) == 1


def test_does_not_touch_similar_names():
    src = "pydantic-settings==1.0\npydantic_core==2.0\npydantic>=1.8,<2\n"
    out, ch = bump_text(src, "pydantic", SPEC, "requirements.txt")
    assert "pydantic-settings==1.0" in out
    assert "pydantic_core==2.0" in out
    assert "pydantic>=2,<3" in out
    assert len(ch) == 1


def test_setup_py_install_requires():
    src = 'install_requires=["numpy<2", "scipy>=1.7", \'pandas >= 1.3, <2.0\']'
    out, _ = bump_text(src, "numpy", SPEC, "setup.py")
    assert '"numpy>=2,<3"' in out and '"scipy>=1.7"' in out
    out2, _ = bump_text(src, "pandas", SPEC, "setup.py")
    assert "'pandas>=2,<3'" in out2


def test_pep621_pyproject():
    src = '[project]\ndependencies = [\n  "pydantic>=1.10,<2",\n  "httpx",\n]\n'
    out, ch = bump_text(src, "pydantic", SPEC, "pyproject.toml")
    assert '"pydantic>=2,<3"' in out
    assert len(ch) == 1


def test_poetry_string_and_table():
    src = '[tool.poetry.dependencies]\npython = "^3.10"\npydantic = "^1.10"\nnumpy = {version = "^1.24", optional = true}\n'
    out, _ = bump_text(src, "pydantic", "^2", "pyproject.toml")
    assert 'pydantic = "^2"' in out
    out2, _ = bump_text(src, "numpy", "^2", "pyproject.toml")
    assert 'numpy = {version = "^2", optional = true}' in out2


def test_setup_cfg_unquoted():
    src = "[options]\ninstall_requires =\n    numpy>=1.20,<2\n    click\n"
    out, ch = bump_text(src, "numpy", SPEC, "setup.cfg")
    assert "    numpy>=2,<3\n" in out
    assert len(ch) == 1


def test_unpinned_name_gets_constraint():
    out, ch = bump_text("pandas\nnumpy\n", "pandas", SPEC, "requirements.txt")
    assert out.splitlines()[0] == "pandas>=2,<3"
    assert len(ch) == 1


def test_mentions():

    assert not mentions("pydantic-settings==1.0", "pydantic")

        """Copy a local folder in as a fresh git repo (used for examples and local projects)."""
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        root = Path(local_dir)
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=buf, mode="w:gz") as tar:

"""Baseline -> bump -> red, with no model calls. Checks the executor + workspace plumbing."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import time

from greenlight.config import load_env

load_env()

from greenlight.executor import get_executor  # noqa: E402
from greenlight.workspace import Workspace  # noqa: E402

src = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "examples/pydantic-v1-shop"
lib, spec = (sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else ("pydantic", ">=2,<3")

ex = get_executor("docker")
t0 = time.monotonic()
with ex.open() as sb:
    ws = Workspace(sb)
    if src.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        ws.clone(src)
    else:
        ws.upload(src)
    p = ws.detect()
    print("manifests:", p.manifests, "| python:", p.python)
    print("install:", p.install_cmds)
    r = ws.install()
    print("install ok:", r.ok, f"{time.monotonic() - t0:.0f}s")
    if not r.ok:
        print(r.output[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)
    print(lib, "before:", ws.installed_version(lib))
    base = ws.run_tests()
    print("BASELINE:", base.summary(), f"{base.duration_s:.1f}s")
    if base.collection_error:
        print(base.collection_error[-2000:])

    print("bump:", ws.bump(lib, spec))
    r = ws.install()
    print("re-install ok:", r.ok)
    if not r.ok:
        print(r.output[-3000:])
    print(lib, "after:", ws.installed_version(lib))
    after = ws.run_tests()
    print("AFTER BUMP:", after.summary())
    if after.collection_error:
        print("collection error tail:\n", after.collection_error[-2500:])
    for k, v in list(after.failures.items())[:6]:
        print(" -", k, "|", v.splitlines()[0][:160] if v else "")
    print(f"total {time.monotonic() - t0:.0f}s")
